prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity desktop portfolio landing-page direction comp, 1536 by 1024 landscape
Primary request: Design an actual responsive website viewport for COLTON SPURGIN as a field archive: a life in progress reconstructed from evidence instead of sales claims. The visitor must quickly understand who Colton is, what he has done, and whether his working style fits them.
Scene/backdrop: no scene; this is a flat front-facing website screenshot on a continuous archival work surface
Subject: a candid personal portfolio for an Air Force NCO, lead software developer intern, research assistant, and UWF senior specializing in AI who graduates December 2026 and wants to build useful ambitious software before pursuing a master’s degree
Style/medium: high-fidelity editorial web UI combining field notebooks, museum specimen labels, typed archive slips, graphite annotation, and restrained modernist typography; quiet, confident, trustworthy
Composition/framing: a narrow indexed top rail with COLTON SPURGIN at left and 01 WORK, 02 EXPERIENCE, 03 ABOUT, 04 CONTACT at right; beneath it, one dominant left-aligned opening statement, “I BUILD SYSTEMS, LEARN HARD PROBLEMS, AND CARE ABOUT DOING USEFUL WORK WELL.”; alongside the statement place a compact identity ledger listing AIR FORCE NCO, LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN, RESEARCH ASSISTANT, AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026. The second fold begins within the same viewport as a continuous evidence table with four horizontal artifact rows for BORK, VELLM, TSP BENCHMARKS, and HOME LAB. Give every artifact a small index and status line. Make one rust-red review mark crossing the headline the single dominant signature move; keep the archive structure calm and exact.
Color palette: warm uncoated paper #e8e1d2, ink #252821, rust #a84b32, field gray-green #6b725f
Materials/textures: subtle real paper grain, typed labels, graphite registration marks, one red-pencil review stroke
Text (verbatim): “COLTON SPURGIN”; “01 WORK”; “02 EXPERIENCE”; “03 ABOUT”; “04 CONTACT”; “I BUILD SYSTEMS, LEARN HARD PROBLEMS, AND CARE ABOUT DOING USEFUL WORK WELL.”; “AIR FORCE NCO”; “LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN”; “RESEARCH ASSISTANT”; “AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026”; “SELECTED EVIDENCE”; “BORK”; “VELLM”; “TSP BENCHMARKS”; “HOME LAB”; “VIEW THE WORK”; “START A CONVERSATION”
Constraints: this must read unmistakably as a usable desktop website, not a poster or museum exhibit; all core UI text must be legible; factual and restrained; no portrait photo; no logo; no invented employers, metrics, awards, testimonials, or project claims
Avoid: generic SaaS cards, bento grid, neon cyber aesthetic, terminal UI, 3D mockup, browser chrome, decorative laptop or phone, illegible pseudo-text, gradients, rounded pill buttons, heavy shadows, watermark
